Swiss Army Bench 0.0.26

- **Projects has a page of its own.** The red mark is the first item on the rail, on every page and window, and
  opens **Projects**: your projects, New project, Open project and the tour. The app opens there; the grid page is
  only the grids. The rail's icons are a little smaller, so more fit, and APIs sits right after Connections.
- **A variable anywhere a value is typed.** Type `${NAME}` in any box (a connection's server or password, an API's
  address, a file path, a setting, a SQL query) and it reads that variable from the Variables page when it is used,
  so the value stays out of shared files and each computer fills in its own. Typing `${` offers your variables;
  right-click any box for **Insert variable…**. A connection's fields are one box each now: the source, vault and
  entry drop-downs are gone. In SQL a variable is sent as a safe parameter. Your saved connections' passwords move
  to variables of the same name once (a backup is kept). `$${NAME}` types the text itself.
- **Join a team.** Settings has one **Team** box: Join a team… (sign in to GitHub, pick your team's repository,
  done) or Start a team…. One repository holds the team library (connections, variables, blades, the shared
  catalog) and the shared projects. After joining it is one row: Pull, Push, Set up this computer, Leave.
- **What is loading is locked and says so.** While a panel, card, tree or form loads, it is covered with readable
  words and cannot be clicked; buttons that start slow work stay busy until it ends.
- **Every error looks the same:** in place where it happened, what happened, where, the fix as a button, Details
  with Copy, and Send to the agent.
- **The desktop app:**
  - Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+T work on tabs (Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the last closed table).
  - **Open with Swiss Army Bench** for .csv, .parquet, .xlsx, .ipynb and .blade.py (never the default program);
    a file always opens in the running app. A file dropped on a window keeps its real path.
  - A table whose file changed on disk says so, with **Reload** (its steps kept) and **Not now**.
  - A table sent from Python opens in the app when VS Code is not open.
  - Faster start, no freezes when a page opens or closes, a clean quit for updates and `swissarmybench stop`, and
    Print to PDF uses the page's paper size.
- **The tour** goes to each page and lights up the real control, with practice tables it removes afterwards, and
  two hands-on steps: type `${` in a box, and right-click one.
- **Sign in with GitHub** says in plain words why GitHub refused (for example, the app's Enable Device Flow box).
